questions.question: Work out 4,75 × 10 and 4,75 × 100, and say what happens to the digits.
questions.expected_answer: 4,75 times 10 gives 47,5, because every digit moves one place to the left. 4,75 times 100 gives 475, because every digit moves two places to the left.

questions.question: Explain why 4,75 × 10 is not 4,750.
questions.expected_answer: 4,750 has the same value as 4,75, because a zero at the end of a decimal changes nothing. Multiplying by 10 must make the number ten times bigger, so the digits move one place to the left to give 47,5.

questions.question: Change 2,45 m to centimetres. Explain why you multiply.
questions.expected_answer: There are 100 cm in 1 m, and centimetres are smaller, so there will be more of them. Multiply by 100 and the digits move two places to the left: 2,45 m is 245 cm.
